===== ec9d161 Marcel Angelo Navarro 2026-08-22
fix(registry): make union prop resolution order-independent and fail closed

Two defects in 13add6e's union handling, both reproduced before fixing.

Partial unions were published as complete. `.filter(Boolean)` dropped members
declared in other files and the bail-out only fired when every member failed,
so `A | B` with an external B resolved to A's props alone — and with
members.length shrunk to 1, every surviving prop satisfied the
present-in-every-member test and was reported required. Now all-or-nothing:
if any member is unresolvable the union expression is returned.

Requiredness depended on declaration order. Optionality was inferred from
presence count and the first member's text was kept verbatim, so a prop that
one variant makes optional could be published as mandatory. Reversing
ZimmButton's operands turned `variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'` into
`variant: 'icon'` — the same false-requiredness claim 13add6e set out to fix,
relocated. A prop is now required only where every member carries it and every
member declares it without `?`, and types are unioned across members instead
of taken from whichever operand came first.

Within a member an intersection may declare a prop twice (the base's
`label: string` plus the member's own literal); `A & B` must satisfy both, so
the member requires the prop if any declaration does.

ZimmButton is the only affected row: variant and size now show their full
unions, `label` stays required, and the `?` markers are stable under operand
reversal. Generator remains idempotent.

===== 13add6e Marcel Angelo Navarro 2026-08-22
fix(registry): resolve union-alias props instead of merging variants

extractTsProps' block regex requires an object-literal body, so a union
alias (`type ZimmButtonProps = ZimmLabelButtonProps | ZimmIconButtonProps`)
never matched and fell through to the merge-everything fallback. That
flattened both variants into one row, presenting mutually-exclusive props
as co-required: ZimmButton advertised `label: string` alongside a required
`icon: ZimmIconType`, a combination the type forbids.

Detect the union alias for the preferred type, resolve its members, and
mark any prop absent from at least one member optional — which is what `?`
means at a union. Resolution follows one level of intersection because both
members are `ZimmButtonBaseProps & {...}`, and reading only their own
literals dropped the shared `label` entirely. Members declared in another
file yield the union expression rather than the misreporting merge.

Net registry effect is `icon:` -> `icon?:`; no other row changes and the
generator stays idempotent. Left in the file's existing no-semicolon style:
scripts/ is outside `npm run lint`'s overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx} scope and HEAD
already carries 369 prettier-rule errors, so reformatting would add ~370
lines of unrelated churn to an ungated file.

===== 712065f Marcel Angelo Navarro 2026-08-21
fix(registry): escape angle brackets outside code spans and match extended Props types

escapeCell only escaped the pipe. Bare angle brackets are the same hazard — GitHub parses
`Array<Foo>` in a table cell as raw HTML and drops it, so `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>`
rendered as `React.Ref`. Escaping them blanket would have been a regression: inside a code
span GFM already shows `<` literally and does not decode entities, so `` `<picture>` ``
would have rendered as visible `<picture>`. Verified with a GFM parser — 4 of the 8
real occurrences are inside backticks. Splitting on the code-span pattern escapes only the
bare ones.

extractTsProps' block regex allowed only whitespace or `=` between the type name and its
opening brace, so `extends BoxProps` and `= BoxProps &` matched nothing and the
preferredTypeName lookup fell into the merge-everything fallback it exists to prevent.
Button and PageContainer were emitting an empty props cell; ZimmButton was silently
dropping two variant types.

Also re-indents the two-pass loop added in 706e47d, whose body was never shifted, leaving
the closing braces stacked. Generator output is byte-identical, and nothing lints .mjs.

The pre-commit hook regenerates the Claude Code registry unconditionally,
and each full regen recomputed a repo-wide grep-based consumers count for
every row (~150 subprocess calls, dominated by ~130 base-template rows)

its own file's content changes. lastTouched stays uncached since it's
cheap and self-corrects the pre-commit one-commit-lag on its own.

---

# The `.claude/registry/` component registry

## 1. What it is and who consumes it

A set of five generated Markdown tables under `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/.claude/registry/` that inventory every component, hook, utility, page, and route in the app — **both the Zimmermann overrides and the inherited `@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0` base template**, merged into one table each, with an `Origin` column (`Base` / `Override` / `Custom`) distinguishing them.

The problem it solves is stated in the script's own header at `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:1-16`:

```js
 * Scans components, hooks, utils, and pages under overrides/app/ and writes
 * structured markdown tables that Claude Code reads instead of grepping the
 * codebase.
```

**The consumer is Claude, not humans and not CI.** Concretely:

- `.claude/skills/feature-spec/SKILL.md:37-41` — "Agent A — Registry / file scan: _If `.claude/registry/` exists_, read `.claude/registry/components.md`, `hooks.md`, and `utils.md`. _Otherwise_, do a direct scan: `find overrides/app/components ... -type f` and grep". The registry is explicitly the cheap substitute for a filesystem sweep.
- `.claude/skills/generate-changelog/SKILL.md:49-53` — "Agent C — New components / hooks scan: If `.claude/registry/` exists, run `git diff [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .claude/registry/` and parse for new entries". Here the registry's *git history* is the changelog source.
- The mirrored copies at `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md:40` and `:796` mean Copilot/Cursor get the same instruction.
- `coderabbit.yaml:57-58` explicitly **excludes** it from AI PR review: `# Generated by scripts/generateRegistry.mjs from overrides/app/` / `- "!.claude/registry/*.md"` — i.e. it is treated as build output, not reviewable source.

Beyond "what exists", each row also carries governance metadata Claude needs before editing: `Tier` (1 Frozen / 2 Protected / 4 Feature-local) and `Squad` (A / B / Shared), derived from hardcoded path lists at `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:119-209` that mirror `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md`. Plus `Consumers` (blast radius) and `Last touched`.

**Notable gap:** neither `AGENTS.md` nor any file in `.claude/rules/` nor anything in `.docs/` mentions the registry at all. Its only documentation is the script header, the two skills above, and `scripts/hooks/README.md:5`. A developer reading the governance docs would not know it exists.

## 2. How it's generated

**Parsing method: hand-rolled regex on raw file text. No AST, no TypeScript compiler API, no Babel.** The script has zero parsing dependencies — its entire import list is `fs`, `path`, `url`, `child_process`, `crypto` (`scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:18-22`). Everything is `String.matchAll` / `RegExp.exec` over `readFileSync(..., 'utf-8')`. The consequences of that choice run through every convention in §6.

The main extractors:

| Extractor | Line | Technique |
|---|---|---|
| `extractDescription` | `:283` | Strips whole-line `//` comments, then regex-scans `/\*\*([\s\S]*?)\*\//g`; two passes — first requires the JSDoc's following declaration to be named the row's own subject, second falls back to "first qualifying JSDoc" |
| `extractTsProps` | `:436` | `/(?:type\|interface)\s+(\w*Props)\s*(?:=\s*)?([^{\n]*)\{([\s\S]*?)\n\}/g` for blocks, then per-line `/^\s{2,}(\w+)(\??):\s*(.+?)\s*[;,]?\s*$/gm` |
| `extractPropTypes` | `:381` | `/^ {4}(\w+)\s*:\s*PropTypes\.(\w+)([\s\S]*?)(?=\n {4}\w\|\n\})/gm` — literally 4-space-indented lines only, for legacy `.jsx` |
| `extractExports` | `:563` | `/^export\s+(?:const\|function\|async\s+function)\s+(\w+)/gm` |
| `parseRoutesFile` | `:1054` | `loadable(() => import('...'))` name→folder map, then `/\{\s*path:\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"][^}]*?component:\s*(\w+)/g` |
| `countConsumers` | `:593` | shells out to `grep -rl "<stem>" overrides/app --include=... \| grep -v .test. \| wc -l` |
| `getLastTouched` | `:574` | shells out to `git log -1 --format=%cs -- "<path>"` |

**Sources walked — both.** Overrides come from `APP = overrides/app` (`:27`); the base template comes from `BASE_APP = node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app` (`:29`), scanned by `scanBaseComponents`/`scanBaseHooks`/`scanBaseUtils`/`scanBasePages` at `:612-701`. The two are merged by folder-name key, with `folderVariants()` (`:110`) trying kebab↔camel spellings, and the match determines `Origin`:

```js
const baseMatch = [...folderVariants(dir)].map((v) => baseByKey.get(v)).find(Boolean)
if (baseMatch) baseByKey.delete(baseMatch.key)
...
origin: baseMatch ? 'Override' : 'Custom',
```
(`scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:764-768`) — the `delete` means a matched base row is consumed and does not re-emit as its own `Base` row.

**The two-cache split** (both gitignored — `.gitignore:63-64`; only the five `.md` files are tracked):

- **`.baseCache.json`** (52 KB) — caches the *entire base-template scan*, keyed by two invalidators: `{version: <retail-react-app version>, schema: BASE_CACHE_SCHEMA, components: [...], hooks: [...], utils: [...], pages: [...]}`. Currently `version: "10.0.0"`, `schema: 3`, holding 73 components / 57 hooks / 30 utils / 15 pages. Rows look like `{"key":"_app","name":"App","path":"app/components/_app/index.jsx","props":"—","desc":"—","consumers":5}`. `loadBaseCache()` (`:91`) returns `null` — forcing a full rescan — if either the package version or the schema number differs. Rationale: base files can only change when the npm package changes, so the ~130 `grep`+parse operations need to run once per package version, not once per commit.
- **`.overrideCache.json`** (3.8 KB) — a much narrower cache: *only the `consumers` count*, and only for `components` and `hooks` (the two registries with a Consumers column). Keyed by repo-relative path, storing a content hash alongside: `{"overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx": {"hash":"a016a9f6…","consumers":6}}`. 19 component + 7 hook entries today. `cachedConsumers` (`:736`) reuses the count when the sha1 of the file's own content is unchanged. Its documented tradeoff, `:729-734`:

  > Tradeoff: a row's count only updates when *that row's own file* changes — not when some other file starts/stops referencing it. Use `--fresh` to force a full recompute…

Both caches exist purely as a performance fix — commit `42e32dc` (`perf(registry): cache consumers counts to avoid full re-scan on every commit`, TimLavelleACC, 2026-07-06): "each full regen recomputed a repo-wide grep-based consumers count for every row (~150 subprocess calls…) even when nothing relevant had changed. This also caused spurious column drift."

**Three invocation modes** (`:1163-1188`): no args = full regen of all five; `--file=PATH` = incremental, routes to exactly one generator by path substring and skips the expensive `consumers`/`lastTouched` columns (they emit `—`); `--fresh` = full regen ignoring both caches.

## 4. Freshness — enforced locally, nowhere in CI

**There is no drift check.** No CI workflow runs `generateRegistry.mjs` or diffs its output — `grep -rn "registry" .github/workflows/` returns nothing. There is no `--check` mode, no `git diff --exit-code` gate. A commit made with `--no-verify`, or via the GitHub web UI, or by any tool that doesn't run husky, leaves the registry silently stale with no signal.

What *does* exist is a **local pre-commit auto-regenerate-and-stage**, at `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:44-62` (wired via husky — `.husky/pre-commit` is one line, `bash scripts/hooks/pre-commit`):

```bash
staged=$(git diff --cached --name-only)

registry_components=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/components/' || true)
registry_hooks=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/hooks/' || true)
registry_utils=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/utils/' || true)
registry_pages=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/pages/' || true)
registry_routes=$(echo "$staged" | grep -E '^overrides/app/routes\.(tsx|jsx)$' || true)

if [ -n "$registry_components$registry_hooks$registry_utils$registry_pages$registry_routes" ] \
  && command -v node &>/dev/null && [ -f "scripts/generateRegistry.mjs" ]; then
  echo "Regenerating Claude Code registry..."
  node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs
  git add .claude/registry/
fi
```

Note this **never fails the commit** — it regenerates and stages, so drift is repaired rather than blocked. It only fires when a file under one of those four dirs (or `routes.tsx`) is staged.

Two other refresh paths:

- **Claude's own PostToolUse hook** — `.claude/settings.json` registers `.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh` on `Edit|Write`, which calls `"$NODE_BIN" scripts/generateRegistry.mjs --file="$file_path"` (`.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh:45`) after scoping to `overrides/app/{components,hooks,utils,pages}/` or `routes.*` and skipping `.test.`/`.stories.`/`ContentfulDefinition` files (`:23-31`). This is the incremental mode, so it deliberately leaves `Consumers` and `Last touched` as `—` until the next full run.
- **`postinstall`** — `package.json:53`: `"postinstall": "npm run compile-translations && … && npm run generate:registry"`, with `"generate:registry": "node scripts/generateRegistry.mjs"` at `:54`. This is what refreshes `.baseCache.json` after an `npm install` bumps the retail-react-app version.

Timestamp churn is suppressed by `writeIfChanged` (`:229-238`), which strips the `> Last updated:` line before comparing, so a no-op regen doesn't dirty the tree.

**The registry is stale right now**, which demonstrates the gap concretely. On this branch, `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` and six new `ui-kits` components are staged, but:
- `.claude/registry/pages.md:20` still reads `| ProductDetail | Base | \`app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx\` |` — the override doesn't exist as far as the registry knows.
- `grep -c "| ZimmProductName |" components.md` → 0, likewise `ZimmProductPrice`, `ZimmProductDescription`, `ZimmProductContent`.
- `routes.md` header says `Last updated: 2026-07-28`, while `overrides/app/routes.tsx` is modified and staged.

This is expected — the hook fires at commit time, not at stage time — but it means anything reading the registry mid-session sees the pre-change world.

### The two "union prop resolution" / "fail closed" commits

**Setup.** `ZimmButton` is a discriminated union, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx:10-33`:

```ts
type ZimmButtonBaseProps = { … label: string; type?: 'button' | 'submit' | 'reset'; … }
type ZimmLabelButtonProps = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'; size?: 'large' | 'medium'; … }
type ZimmIconButtonProps  = ZimmButtonBaseProps & { variant: 'icon'; icon: ZimmIconType; size?: ZimmIconSize; … }
type ZimmButtonProps = ZimmLabelButtonProps | ZimmIconButtonProps;
```

**Bug 1, fixed by `13add6e`.** `extractTsProps`'s block regex requires an object-literal body (`…\{([\s\S]*?)\n\}`). A union alias has no `{`, so `ZimmButtonProps` never matched, the `preferredTypeName` lookup found nothing, and execution fell through to the merge-everything fallback at `:552-565` — flattening *both* variants into one row. Per the commit body: "ZimmButton advertised `label: string` alongside a required `icon: ZimmIconType`, a combination the type forbids." The fix added the union-alias branch at `:475`:

```js
const alias = new RegExp(`type\\s+${preferredTypeName}\\s*=\\s*([^;{]+);`).exec(content)
if (alias && alias[1].includes('|')) {
```
plus `resolveProps` (`:484-495`), which follows intersection ancestors — necessary because each member is `ZimmButtonBaseProps & {…}` and reading only its own literal dropped the shared `label` entirely.

**Bug 2 — two defects in that fix, both fixed by `ec9d161`.** The commit body: "Two defects in 13add6e's union handling, both reproduced before fixing."

*(a) Partial unions published as complete — the "fail closed" half.* `13add6e` used `.filter(Boolean)` and only bailed if *every* member failed to resolve. So for `A | B` where `B` is declared in another file, `B` was silently dropped, `A`'s props became the whole union — and worse, because `members.length` had shrunk to 1, "present in every member" was trivially satisfied and **every surviving prop was published as required**. A partial parse produced a confidently wrong, more-restrictive-looking row. Now it is all-or-nothing (`:496-500`):

```js
// All-or-nothing: a member declared in another file can't be resolved from this content, and
// publishing the members that did resolve would present a partial union as a complete one —
// worse, with `members.length` shrunk to match, every surviving prop would satisfy the
// present-in-every-member test below and be reported required. Surface the union expression.
const resolved = memberNames.map((name) => allBlocks.find(({typeName}) => typeName === name))
if (resolved.some((block) => !block)) return [memberNames.join(' | ')]
```

The cell then honestly reads `ZimmLabelButtonProps | ZimmIconButtonProps` rather than a fabricated prop list.

*(b) Requiredness depended on declaration order.* `13add6e` inferred optionality from a *presence count* and kept the first member's text verbatim. The commit body's reproduction: "Reversing ZimmButton's operands turned `variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'` into `variant: 'icon'` — the same false-requiredness claim 13add6e set out to fix, relocated." The fix separates presence from optionality and unions the types (`:526-540`):

```js
// At the union a prop is required only where every member carries it *and* every member
// declares it without `?` — presence alone isn't enough, or a prop that one variant makes
// optional gets published as mandatory. Types are unioned across members rather than taken
// from whichever member happened to be declared first, so the row no longer depends on the
// order of the alias' operands.
const carriedByAll = memberFacts.every((facts) => facts.has(name))
const requiredByAll = carriedByAll && memberFacts.every((facts) => facts.get(name).required)
…
unionProps.push(`${name}${requiredByAll ? '' : '?'}: ${types.join(' | ')}`)
```

It also handles within-member intersections declaring the same prop twice — `A & B` must satisfy both, so the member requires it if *any* declaration does (`:504-524`).

**Resulting behaviour today**, visible in `.claude/registry/components.md:86`: `label: string` (required — in both members, unmarked in both), `variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'icon'` and `size?: 'large' | 'medium' | ZimmIconSize` (types unioned across members, optional because one member marks them optional), `icon?: ZimmIconType` (optional — absent from the label variant). Both commits assert the generator stays idempotent and ZimmButton was the only row affected.

## 6. Conventions a new component must follow to be indexed correctly

This is entirely regex-driven, so the rules are literal and unforgiving. Nothing warns you when a component is silently missed — it just doesn't appear.

### Components

**(a) Must be `index.tsx` (or `index.jsx`) in its own folder.** `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs:746-750`:

```js
const files = findFiles(
    join(APP, 'components'),
    ['.jsx', '.tsx'],
    ['.test.', '.stories.', '/shared/ui']
  ).filter((f) => basename(f).startsWith('index.'))
```
A component at `components/foo/foo.tsx` is invisible. `findFiles` recurses, so nested layouts like `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/index.tsx` work fine. Note `'.ts'` is **not** in the extension list, so a non-JSX `index.ts` component/barrel is never scanned (the `file.endsWith('.ts')` check at `:760` is unreachable dead code). This matches `.claude/rules/conventions.md`'s folder-layout rule, but the registry is the thing that *silently punishes* deviation.

**(b) The row's name comes from the folder name, not the exported symbol.** `:757-758`:
```js
const dir = basename(dirname(file))
const name = toPascalCase(dir)
```
`toPascalCase` (`:240-246`) strips leading underscores and splits on `-` only. So `zimmButton/` → `ZimmButton`, `_app-config/` → `AppConfig`. If your folder is named one thing and your export another, the registry shows the folder's name. Also: **components.md does not dedupe by name** (unlike hooks.md at `:911-916`) — two folders with the same leaf name anywhere in the tree produce two identically-named rows.

**(c) The props type must be named exactly `<PascalFolderName>Props` and live in the same file.** `:759-762`:
```js
const props = file.endsWith('.tsx') || file.endsWith('.ts')
      ? extractTsProps(content, `${name}Props`)
      : extractPropTypes(content)
```
`extractTsProps` only ever sees `content` — the single file's text. **Props moved to a sibling `types.ts` are invisible**, and since `.claude/rules/components.md` explicitly sanctions moving them there once shared with a story/test, following that rule blanks the Props column. When the preferred name isn't found, it falls back to merging *every* `*Props` block in the file (`:552-565`) — which is exactly the leak `fe128fd` fixed for `Footer`, so a mis-named props type re-opens it: internal sub-component props get published as the public component's API.

**(d) Formatting of the type declaration matters.** Block regex, `:444`:
```js
const re = /(?:type|interface)\s+(\w*Props)\s*(?:=\s*)?([^{\n]*)\{([\s\S]*?)\n\}/g
```
The `[^{\n]*` cannot cross a newline, so the opening `{` must be on the **same line** as the type name. The terminating `\n}` must be a closing brace at **column 0**, so a `Props` type nested inside anything indented won't terminate correctly. Field regex, `:453`:
```js
const lineRe = /^\s{2,}(\w+)(\??):\s*(.+?)\s*[;,]?\s*$/gm
```
Fields need **≥2 leading spaces** (a zero- or one-space-indented field is skipped) and must be one-per-line — a multi-line type expression only contributes its first line. `children` is always dropped (`:456-457`).

**(e) Union-alias props types must have their members declared in the same file**, or the whole cell degrades to the union expression (see §5). Intersection ancestors are resolved for union members only — deliberately, per the comment at `:481-483`.

**(f) The Description comes from a JSDoc `/** */` immediately above a top-level declaration *named the same as the row*.** `:308-321`:
```js
const isDeclaration =
  /^\s*(import\s|(export\s+)?(default\s+)?(async\s+)?(function|const|let|var|class|interface|type|enum)\s)/.test(nextLine)
if (!isDeclaration) continue

// First pass only: the declaration must be the row's own subject.
if (requireName) {
  const declared = nextLine.match(/(?:function|const|let|var|class|interface|type|enum)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/)
  if (!declared || declared[1] !== preferredName) continue
}
```
So `/** … */ export const ZimmButton = …` works. Copyright/SPDX blocks are skipped (`:305`). `@summary` wins if present (`:325-329`). The description is truncated to ~200 chars on a sentence boundary. If no JSDoc names the component, pass 2 grabs the first qualifying JSDoc in the file — which is how `footer/index.tsx`'s `leavesTheSite` helper hijacked the Footer row before `706e47d`. **Practical rule: JSDoc the exported component itself, not a helper above it.**

**(g) A `.jsx` component uses `.propTypes` with exactly 4-space indentation** (`:387`: `/^ {4}(\w+)\s*:\s*PropTypes\.(\w+)…/gm`). Prettier's default 2-space indent would break this — only relevant for base-template files, but it means base rows can silently show `—`.

### Hooks

Filename stem must match `/^use[-A-Z]/` — `use-foo.ts` or `useFoo.ts`, never `usefoo.ts` (`:830`, `:642`). Only `.ts`/`.js`; a `.tsx` hook file is invisible. Only **two directory levels** are accepted (`:833-847`): top-level `useFoo.ts`, `useFoo/index.ts`, or `useFoo/useBar.ts`. Anything deeper is dropped. Names are deduped globally with override rows first (`:911-916`), so a custom hook colliding with a base hook name shadows the base row.

### Utils

`overrides/app/utils/*.{js,ts}`, excluding anything starting with `index` and anything matching `.test.` / `.stories.` / `test-utils` (`:928-932`). **`.tsx` is not in the extension list** — and this is currently biting: `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` is staged on this branch and `grep -c richText .claude/registry/utils.md` → **0**. It can never appear.

The Exports column regex (`:565`) is `^export\s+(?:const|function|async\s+function)\s+(\w+)` — so `export type`, `export class`, `export default`, and `export {foo}` re-export forms are **not** captured, and names starting with `_` are filtered (`:566`). Exports must be declared inline at column 0.

### Pages

One directory level under `overrides/app/pages/` (`readdirSync`, `:993`), containing `index.tsx` or `index.jsx`. Nested page folders (`checkout/payment-processing/`) appear in `routes.md` but never get their own `pages.md` row.

### Routes

`parseRoutesFile` (`:1054-1078`) needs two literal shapes. Loadable: `const X = loadable(() => import('...'))` — an inline `component: loadable(...)`, a variable indirection, or a template-literal path all fail. Route object: `/\{\s*path:\s*['"]…['"][^}]*?component:\s*(\w+)/g` — `path` must come **before** `component`, both must be string/identifier literals, and `[^}]*?` means no nested `}` may sit between them. Base-route inheritance is only detected for the exact form `import {routes as Alias} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes'` + `...Alias` (`:1103-1118`).

### Tier / Squad classification

`getTier`/`getSquad` (`:199-209`) are naive `relPath.includes(p)` substring tests against hardcoded arrays at `:119-197`. Two consequences: the lists are a **hand-maintained duplicate** of `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` / `protectedFiles.md` with no sync check, and they only know base-template kebab-case paths. Everything under `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**` therefore classifies as `4 — Feature-local` / `Shared` regardless of what it actually is — which is why all ten `Zimm*` rows carry that pair.

## Summary of gaps found

1. **No CI drift gate.** Freshness depends entirely on a husky pre-commit hook that auto-stages rather than blocks; `--no-verify`, web-UI commits, or a missing `node` all bypass it silently. There is no `--check` mode to wire up.
2. **`.tsx` utilities are unreachable** — `overrides/app/utils/richText.tsx` is staged today and cannot ever appear in `utils.md` (`:929-932`).
3. **`.claude/rules/components.md`'s "move props to `types.ts`" guidance silently blanks the Props column**, because `extractTsProps` only reads the single file.
4. **Tier/Squad path lists are a hand-maintained copy** of the governance rules with no sync test, and don't cover the `ui-kits/` tree at all.
5. **The registry is undocumented in `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/rules/`, and `.docs/`** — only the script header, two skills, and `scripts/hooks/README.md:5` mention it.
6. **`components.md` doesn't dedupe by row name** (hooks.md does), so leaf-folder name collisions across the tree would produce duplicate rows.
